targets.text: lobes lanes boot, compile and run safely: GPU services hold after a power cycle, the vLLM compile cache survives a recreate, a hot box sheds load instead of power-cycling, and clocks stay stock outside an explicit benchmark window
Every clause of the announcement maps to a merged PR in the stack (boot hold, compile cache, backoff + cache clear, thermal shedding, benchmark window) with its tests green

Thor carries experimental work: this effort may change code, templates, tests, docs and goldens, but must NOT deploy, recreate or restart anything on the Thor; live Thor validation is deferred and stays DECLARED/UNVALIDATED (#108)
No step in the delivery runs docker, compose or lobes write verbs against the Thor; Thor-facing claims are marked DECLARED/UNVALIDATED in docs

mg-logwrap.sh holds before its final exec until host uptime (/proc/uptime, not namespaced) >= LOBES_BOOT_DELAY_S (default 120, 0 = off), logging the hold; read with bash builtins (no cut/awk dependency); exec "$@" stays last so signals and exit codes are unchanged
A unit test runs mg-logwrap with a fake uptime source: below the delay it sleeps the remainder; at/after the delay or with LOBES_BOOT_DELAY_S=0 it does not sleep; exec stays the last statement
restart: unless-stopped stays on every service (it is the only policy in every template today, no on-failure anywhere); the boot hold is what makes auto-restart safe, not a policy change
grep over every template and the shape renderer finds restart: unless-stopped on every service and no new restart policy introduced

Healthcheck start_period is raised to cover the boot hold on every wrapped lane (vLLM lanes are 600s today) so a held container is not marked unhealthy, or the hold is shown to fit inside the existing start_period
Every held service's start_period >= its pre-change start_period + LOBES_BOOT_DELAY_S default, or a test proves the hold fits inside it

Every GPU service and the gateway honours the 120 s hold, including services that do not use mg-logwrap today (audio chatterbox/stt, embed-gemma2-embed, decider sidecars, comfyui, gateway): each receives LOBES_BOOT_DELAY_S and runs the hold in its own entrypoint
A test enumerates every service across fleet/single/embed/audio/audio-he templates and the decider sidecar renderer and asserts each one runs the hold before its real entrypoint

Template tests updated: test_cli_logs test_logwrap_template_shipped_and_safe gains assertions for the hold (default 120, 0 disables, exec stays last); tests/test_upgrade_compat fixtures refreshed deliberately if compose bytes change
uv run pytest -n auto passes with the updated logwrap/compose assertions and any refreshed upgrade_compat fixtures committed deliberately

Every vLLM lane persists its compile cache across a recreate: VLLM_CACHE_ROOT (or /root/.cache/vllm) bind-mounted to a per-lane host dir under the deployment (single + fleet templates, embed overlay vLLM lanes), so a compose recreate reuses the known-good torch.compile/inductor artifacts instead of recompiling
Every vLLM service in every template mounts a per-lane compile-cache dir and sets VLLM_CACHE_ROOT to it; a test asserts it

The compile cache is keyed so it cannot be reused across a different image/model/knob set by accident (vLLM's own hash key or a per-lane, per-image subdir), and an operator can wipe it (documented path; a lobes verb is optional)
The cache path includes a per-lane component and vLLM's own content hash still keys entries; docs name the wipe path

Crash backoff (Option C): before exec, mg-logwrap (1) records the start in a per-lane file under the host-mounted log dir and, after N starts inside a window, holds with a logged reason and a documented clear path; (2) waits until host MemAvailable covers the lane's --gpu-memory-utilization share of MemTotal (parsed from its own argv), logging while it waits, with a bounded timeout

Unit tests drive the wrapper with fake /proc/meminfo, fake argv and a fake start log: gate waits until MemAvailable >= share then execs; times out with a logged reason; counter holds after N starts in the window and resets after a clean window

lobes never clears caches from inside a container and never uses full sudo: the clear runs host-side only, through a single NOPASSWD sudoers rule for '/usr/sbin/sysctl -w vm.drop_caches=3' (mjolnir cachectl pattern), and never prompts — no grant means skip and say so
grep finds no drop_caches/sysctl in any template or container entrypoint, no 'sudo ' without -n in lobes/, and the only sudoers content is the single sysctl rule

The gateway pressure policy gains a fourth shed signal, thermal ('hot'): the hottest /sys/class/thermal zone above a per-card threshold sheds sheddable full tiers with 429 + Retry-After exactly like swap; hand (floor) and NEVER_SHED_ROLES (decider) are always served; X-Lobes-Override still bypasses
decide() with a hot sample sheds cortex/senses/worker/muse/associate with 429 + Retry-After, serves hand and decider, and honours X-Lobes-Override — unit tests for each

sample_pressure() and PressureCache carry a thermal field (hottest zone, m°C) read with stdlib from /sys/class/thermal; absent/unreadable zones degrade to 'no thermal signal', never to shedding; lobes status --pressure and GET /status pressure payload show it
With no readable thermal zone the sample carries thermal=None and decide() never sheds on it; status --pressure and GET /status show the value or 'n/a'

Thermal bands are per-card [host_env] data (e.g. LOBES_THERMAL_SHED_C / resume), with hysteresis; only the Spark has measured values (84/88/91/93.5 °C vs 104.8 °C ACPI trip); Thor/Orin render no threshold (signal off) or a DECLARED value marked unmeasured (#108)
spark.toml carries the measured bands; thor/orin goldens either stay byte-identical or carry values explicitly marked unmeasured; goldens regenerated and committed

Serving lanes are NEVER paused and NEVER docker update'd by any lobes governor: pause freezes in-flight requests, and docker update --cpus is a correlated (unproven) suspect for cudaErrorNotPermitted on GPU containers (#304 comments 2 and 3)
grep over lobes/ finds no docker pause or docker update invoked against a serving lane

The gateway container can read host thermal zones: verify /sys/class/thermal is visible in the unprivileged gateway container on Spark/Orin (Thor deferred), else add an explicit read-only bind mount in the fleet compose gateway service
On the Spark and the Orin, the running gateway container reads /sys/class/thermal (transcript), or the compose adds a read-only bind mount that a test asserts

On the Spark, a sustained full-GPU serving load of >= 30 min completes with the thermal signal live and 0 hard resets; the transcript reports shed count and peak zone temperature (Spark only; Thor deferred)
A Spark transcript under docs/evidence/ shows a sustained full-GPU serving load of >= 30 min with the thermal signal live, peak zone temperature, shed count and 0 hard resets

Every lobes benchmark/measure result records host conditions: nvpmodel -q, jetson_clocks --show (or devfreq cur/min/max), fan profile, hottest zone at start and end — best-effort, skipped cleanly on non-Jetson; extends the existing host block (image, gpu_memory)
A benchmark --json result contains a host.conditions block (power mode, clocks, fan profile, temps start/end) or an explicit unavailable reason per field
lobes doctor gains a jetson_clocks_locked (warn) finding: clocks locked outside a benchmark window (e.g. a crashed run left them locked); skipped when the tool or sysfs is absent
doctor emits jetson_clocks_locked (warn) when the machine CLI reports locked clocks outside a window, and skips with no finding when the CLI/tool is absent — tests for both
No persistent clock or fan change from lobes init, serve, switch or any deployment; production stays stock DVFS + the host's nvfancontrol profile
grep shows no clock/fan mutation in init/serve/switch/up code paths; only the benchmark window calls the lock verbs
Operators of lobes boxes (DGX Spark, Jetson AGX Thor, Jetson AGX Orin) and the agents that run lobes verbs on them in loops; secondarily mesh callers who receive a 429 from a hot box
The spec's user-facing docs (operating-a-deployment, measuring-lane-performance, gateway-fleet) address operators and agents by name

Today: a power-cycled box restarts every lane within ~8 s of dockerd, before ssh is possible; every compose recreate recompiles torch.compile from scratch in the writable layer (2 of 3 fresh Thor compiles hit a device-side assert + Xid 43); a crashed lane restarts immediately into memory the crash still holds; the Spark power-cycled twice under sustained full-GPU load with no lobes thermal awareness; benchmark numbers carry no recorded power mode, clocks or temperatures
Each before-state fact cites an issue (#304/#307/#309) or evidence file

A hung box that brings its own crash straight back cannot be rescued remotely, and a box that power-cycles under load loses in-flight work and evidence; unrecorded clocks make benchmark numbers irreproducible (docs/measuring-lane-performance.md Rule 2 already cost one wrong conclusion)
The why is traceable to #304, #307 and docs/measuring-lane-performance.md Rule 2

After a power cycle every lobes service waits until host uptime >= 120 s; a recreate reuses the lane's compile cache; a repeatedly crashing lane backs off instead of looping into held memory; a box over its per-card thermal threshold sheds sheddable tiers with 429 instead of heating further; lobes benchmark runs inside a locked-clocks window delegated to the machine CLI and always restores stock DVFS, recording conditions in the result
Each after-state clause maps to at least one requirement claim with its own test

lobes benchmark (and measure, when it drives load) wraps its run in a benchmark window that delegates to the machine CLI for the detected card — spark / thor / orin — to store state, lock clocks and fan, and ALWAYS restore (try/finally + signal handling) on success, error or Ctrl-C; with no machine CLI or no privilege it runs unlocked and says so in the result (never silently)
Tests with a fake machine CLI show lock then restore on success, on an exception and on SIGINT; with no CLI the result records unlocked + reason

PRs on dgx-spark-cli, jetson-thor-cli and jetson-orin-cli add the clock/fan window verbs (store / lock / restore / show, JSON output) — on Jetson wrapping jetson_clocks --store/--restore and the nvfancontrol profile; on GB10 whatever lock is accepted (nvidia-smi -lgc is unverified, park v2) — before lobes depends on them
Each machine CLI ships window verbs with --json and a restore that returns to the stored state, released before lobes pins a minimum version

Host-side lobes verbs that start or stop GPU lanes (serve/start, stop, switch, up, fleet up/down, init --apply when it starts lanes) clear the page cache (sync + vm.drop_caches=3) after teardown and before start when the grant exists; a one-time grant verb installs the single sudoers drop-in (0440, visudo-checked, explicit consent); doctor reports a missing grant on unified-memory cards (Spark/Thor/Orin)

Tests with a fake sudo/machine CLI show: granted → clear runs after down and before up, in that order; not granted → no prompt (sudo -n), verb continues and prints the skip; dry-run prints the clear in the plan

lobes ships an opt-in host-side watcher (installed by an explicit lobes verb with --apply, removable, the first host unit lobes installs): it watches for a lane holding in the memory gate (a marker file the wrapper writes in the host-mounted log dir) and runs the granted page-cache clear, rate-limited and logged; without the sudoers grant it only logs; never touches containers (no docker pause/update/restart)

Tests: a gate marker appearing triggers exactly one clear per rate-limit window via the granted command; no grant → log only; the watcher issues no docker command; install is dry-run by default and uninstall removes every file it wrote

The boot hold must not release every lane at the same instant: lanes are staggered (a per-lane offset on top of LOBES_BOOT_DELAY_S, ordered to match each card's measured boot order — e.g. Orin associate-first, Thor gears-first with embed/rerank before worker) and the memory gate re-checks after the stagger, because a synchronized release recreates the documented unified-memory first-boot race

A test shows two lanes on the same card get distinct release times; the per-card order is data (profile/shape), documented with its evidence; a doc note cites the boot-order caveat in docs/machine-profiles.md

Host-side lobes verbs that intentionally (re)start a lane (up, serve, switch, fleet up, init --apply) reset that lane's start counter, so deliberate operator restarts never trip the crash-backoff hold; only unattended (dockerd) restarts accumulate
A test runs the verb path against a fake log dir and asserts the lane's counter file is cleared before compose starts it

Every new runtime behaviour has an env off-switch documented in env.example: LOBES_BOOT_DELAY_S=0, a memory-gate and start-counter disable (or N=0), compile-cache mount opt-out, thermal threshold unset = signal off, watcher uninstall — so a field regression is reverted by editing .env, not by a code rollback
env.example lists each knob with its off value; a test per knob shows the off value restores the pre-change behaviour

A safe rollout path for existing deployments: doctor reports a stale scaffold mg-logwrap.sh (digest differs from the packaged template) and a missing compile-cache mount, and a targeted refresh writes ONLY mg-logwrap.sh (with a backup) — because doctor --fix never rewrites existing files, init --force overwrites the whole compose with no backup, and the Spark's hand-edited compose must never be re-scaffolded
Tests: doctor flags a stale mg-logwrap.sh and a missing cache mount; the refresh writes a .bak and only mg-logwrap.sh; no other file in the deployment dir changes

The compile-cache host dir is created by lobes (init / doctor --fix) owned by the operator before first mount, and the documented wipe works without sudo; otherwise the root container creates it root-owned (the same trap as root-owned logs/, docs/operating-a-deployment.md:48) and growth is unbounded with no size report
A test asserts init creates the cache dir; doctor (or status) reports its size; the wipe procedure in docs runs as the operator

The thermal reader uses a per-card zone selector (host_env, e.g. LOBES_THERMAL_ZONES=tj-thermal on Jetson, acpitz on Spark) and skips zones whose temp read fails (ENODATA) or is implausible, instead of a blind 'hottest of all zones'
Tests with a fake sysfs tree: an ENODATA zone is skipped; the selector picks only named zone types; no matching zone means 'no thermal signal'

Benchmark windows are exclusive per host: a lock file (or the machine CLI's own) makes a second concurrent window refuse or wait, so one run's restore never unlocks clocks under another run, and the stored state is never overwritten by a nested store
A test starts two windows with a fake machine CLI: the second refuses/waits; restore runs once, after the owner finishes

The watcher must be running after a reboot without a login (the exact moment it matters): installed as a system unit (root, explicit consent) or a user unit with linger enabled — the install verb verifies whichever it uses and doctor reports it absent
The install plan shows the unit type and the linger/system check; doctor flags an installed-but-inactive watcher

The grant step detects an existing equivalent NOPASSWD rule (sudo -n -l matching sysctl vm.drop_caches or tee /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches) and reuses it instead of installing a duplicate; Thor already carries /etc/sudoers.d/drop-caches
A test feeds fake 'sudo -n -l' listings: an existing rule is detected and no install is planned; absence plans the single drop-in

A thermal shed is observable mesh-wide: the 429 carries a thermal reason (X-Lobes-Tier-Reason / shed_signal 'thermal'), GET /status pressure includes the thermal reading and signal, and a mesh forward that receives it relays the peer's reason (no silent conversion to a generic busy)
Gateway tests assert the reason header and /status fields for a thermal shed; a mesh-forward test asserts the peer's thermal reason is relayed

risks.text: PR-B cannot merge until dgx-spark-cli / jetson-thor-cli / jetson-orin-cli release the contract verbs; t10 builds against fakes meanwhile
GB10 may accept no clock lock (nvidia-smi -lgc unverified, frame park v2): spark window lock may ship as supported:false, so Spark benchmarks record conditions but run unlocked
VLLM_CACHE_ROOT semantics and compile-cache keying are assumed (approved lapse l1) — if the pinned image keys or locates the cache differently, t8 changes its mount approach before the compose edit

The memory gate compares MemAvailable with util x MemTotal, while vLLM checks CUDA free memory: on Jetson the nvmap pool can make them disagree (frame park v6), so the gate may pass and vLLM still refuse — the start counter remains the backstop
All Thor behaviour (gears-first boot order, gate vs nvmap pool, thor window verbs on real hardware) stays DECLARED/UNVALIDATED — Thor is code-only while its experimental work runs
